Subject: Sparrow Health — post-demo burn profile & peak concurrency

Hi Olivia — great demo earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side. Please confirm any of the numbers below if I misunderstood.

Recap from discovery:
- Primary use: clinical summarization + billing-coding assistant across web and mobile apps.
- Expected MAUs in year 1: 80k–120k with steady growth.
- Typical payload: 1.1k tokens per request (prompt + response average).
- Estimated monthly token burn (working range): 250M–420M tokens.
- Expected steady-state peak TPS: 180–220 (10–15s windows); possible short morning burst to higher values — please confirm.
- Target budget: team indicated ~$7–$10 per 1M tokens as guideline for committed pricing.

Operational asks / constraints you mentioned:
- SOC 2 evidence required for procurement (we have documents ready).
- Need a soft canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 2 weeks before full switch.
- Procurement prefers billing monthly with a PO + 30-day payment terms.

Attachments: sparrow-demo-slide.pdf (slides), sparrow_token_samples.jsonl (sample requests).

Suggested next steps:
1) Jordan to provide 2 pricing scenarios (committed vs on-demand) and a simple cost math table.
2) Olivia to confirm typical monthly tokens and worst-case short burst TPS for mornings (how long/how frequent).
3) If numbers align, prepare a one-page MSA + PO template for procurement.

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if you want to walk through the pricing scenarios.

Thanks,

Thanks Jordan — quick confirmations and clarifications below.

Confirmations:
- Monthly tokens: our analytics team reports a conservative production estimate of ~320M tokens/month after month 1, with goal to hit ~500M by Q2 if adoption accelerates.
- Average tokens/request: 1.05k (we rounded up on the call)

Peak behavior (important):
- Typical daytime peaks: 200–250 TPS sustained for 10–20s during morning surge windows.
- We also observe ultra-short bursts (10–20s) up to ~700 TPS when a scheduled batch job fans out notifications (happens twice daily). Those bursts are brief (2–4 minutes total including ramp).

Budget / pricing note:
- Procurement target range is $6–$9 per 1M tokens for committed volume. If committed pricing requires a 12–24 month lock, procurement will need to see clear SLAs and an exit/cap adjustment.

Can you include in your pricing note: committed vs reserved vs on-demand rates, plus any surcharge for peak burst reservation (if applicable)? Also confirm SOC 2 artifacts and the canary flow you mentioned.

I can share a procurement contact for PO templates if helpful.

—Olivia

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Sparrow Health — post-demo burn profile & peak concurrency

Thanks Olivia — helpful detail. Below are three pragmatic pricing scenarios and how we'd handle the bursts. I attached a CSV (pricing_scenarios.csv) with the same numbers for easy reference.

Summary pricing (per 1M tokens):
- Committed (recommended starter): 300M monthly commit, $6.50 / 1M tokens, 12-month term.
- Reserved (higher throughput cushion): 500M monthly commit, $5.85 / 1M tokens, 12-month term + guaranteed burst pool (see below).
- On-demand (no commit): $12.00 / 1M tokens, pay-as-you-go.

Quick unit-econ math (examples):
- If you run 320M tokens/month on Committed @ $6.50: 320 * $6.50 = $2,080 / month.
- If you run 500M tokens/month on Reserved @ $5.85: 500 * $5.85 = $2,925 / month.
- On-demand 320M @ $12.00: 320 * $12.00 = $3,840 / month.

Peak / burst handling:
- Short 700 TPS bursts: we recommend including a small burst pool with the Reserved plan (applies to ~3–5 minute spikes). For Reserved customers we can allocate a burst capacity buffer (pre-warmed instances) sized to cover 700 TPS for configured short windows — this comes with a small monthly allocation fee that we amortize into the Reserved per-1M price above.
- Canary rollout: we support route-based traffic splitting (5% canary) with automatic rollback on error-rate or latency thresholds — we can run that for 14 days as requested.

Security / procurement:
- SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summary: available on request; will share via secure Drive link once procurement confirms contact.
- Billing: monthly invoicing with PO + 30-day net is fine; we'll include standard SLA terms in the MSA.

Proposed next steps:
1) Olivia/procurement shares expected official monthly commit preference (300M vs 500M) and PO contact.
2) We provision a Reserved burst pool in SFO and schedule a brief technical kickoff with infra to define rate-limit/ramp rules.
3) We exchange a one-page MSA and PO.

If it helps, we can run a 30-day validation POC with $5k of usage credits to validate peak and steady-state behavior before finalizing commit.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a short one-pager and the pricing CSV.

Jordan Blake
